parsed.rationale: Although the two types share structural shape (both are `type-alias-object` with `shared_field_count: 1` and no fields listed), they carry distinct names — `TextHeightPreferenceKey` in `app:WatchXYC` / `WXYC/WatchXYC/PlayerPage.swift` and `ScrollOffsetPreferenceKey` in `app:iOS` / `WXYC/iOS/Views/Playlist/Playcut Detail/PlaycutRowView.swift` — indicating they encode different domain concepts (text height measurement vs. scroll offset tracking) whose structural coincidence is purely incidental. SwiftUI `PreferenceKey` conformances are typically tiny, single-purpose value types that are intentionally co-located with the view that uses them; extracting them to a shared target would couple two unrelated UI concerns and two separate app targets (watchOS and iOS) for no meaningful reuse gain. No restraint markers are present, but the coincidental-shape / divergent-semantics pattern is the operative signal here.
